Night Neighbourhood

Project README

Night Neighbourhood

+

Night Neighbourhood is a small house for two to six university friends who want + company while working on their own tasks. You might be revising quietly, welcome + a short chat, or want help with a confusing paragraph. The house lets those + activities happen together without requiring everyone to post a goal or reply.

+

Quiet company, voluntary conversation

+

Two avatars sitting at the same table tell you that their friends are connected. + They do not tell you whether those people want to talk. Our main design decision + is to keep presence, willingness and room access separate.

+

New arrivals start in Quiet. Choose Can chat when you welcome conversation. + Your friends see that value and when it was set. The time can also come from the + default being initialized; it does not prove that you are watching the screen. + Quiet hides house speech previews while keeping authorized messages and an unread + cue. It is a soft convention, not a message block. The same control currently + changes both public willingness and your previews.

+

An always-open hangout would need less status maintenance and make chance + encounters easier. Invitations accepted before each conversation would make + agreement clearer, but add steps to a brief exchange between familiar friends. + We chose a declaration between those options. Its cost is an extra choice and + the possibility that someone forgets to update it.

+

Erickson and Kellogg (2000) + explain how visibility helps people coordinate while also creating accountability. + Harrison and Dourish (1996) + show why a shared setting needs social meaning beyond its geometry. These ideas + help explain our choices; friends still need to develop and understand the + convention through use.

+

Enter, explore and think together

+

Create a house, share its eight-character code, or join one. A cookie returns you + to the same identity; keep a recovery key private if you want another way back. + Offline members keep their bedroom. Capacity counts residents, not browser tabs.

+

Move with WASD, arrows or touch controls. E uses the nearby door, seat or board. + Follow keeps your avatar in view; Overview and drag inspection give you room + context. Each person can decorate their bedroom with a bounded furniture set. + Bedrooms start closed. Opening one admits current housemates and exposes retained + room chat; visiting does not grant decorating rights. Quiet does not hide your + name, connection or coarse room location.

+

Shared board opens a full canvas with drawing, notes, images and companion chat. + It also works at /board/ independently. Board conversation is house-wide, + separate from room chat. Peers see shared canvas edits and pointer/selection + awareness; each person controls their view. Study cards remain author-controlled. + Saving a next step leaves the card active; closing records the author's choice.

+

What we check and what we still need to learn

+

Ownership, access, saved state, reconnect defaults and delivery are checked in + code and browser journeys. Unconfirmed submitted actions retain their IDs for + retry. Recovery has limits: local-storage failure can leave an unsent board-chat + draft only in memory, outside the pending export.

+

Whether this house feels welcoming, makes asking easier or is preferable to a + well-configured Discord group needs real-friend evaluation. We have not established + a learning benefit. The decision and evidence + explain the alternatives and checks.

+

Built with Three.js, Socket.IO, SQLite and the MIT-licensed Excalidraw editor. + Use the pinned Linux toolchain: pnpm build:board, pnpm start, and pnpm check. + Research and drafting were assisted by AI; the project record is in PROCESS.md.

+
